findings: The baseline runs 6% low across all counties; its ranges caught the real total in 205 of 340 back-test cases.
The baseline runs 13% low in large counties; its ranges caught the real total in 71 of 105 back-test cases.
The baseline runs 23% high in 'Rural, slow-growth, lower-cost' counties; its ranges caught the real total in 58 of 115 back-test cases.
The baseline runs 7% low in urban counties; its ranges caught the real total in 114 of 180 back-test cases.
The baseline runs 7% low in counties with a lower share of Qualified Census Tracts; its ranges caught the real total in 175 of 295 back-test cases.
Its ranges were least reliable in 'Rural, slow-growth, lower-cost' counties: they caught the real total in 58 of 115 cases (50%), against the 80% a P10-P90 range aims for.
by_place.limits: Where the baseline itself has been least accurate in past years: 'Rural, slow-growth, lower-cost' counties (where it has tended to run too high) and small counties (where it has tended to run too high). Read the change in those places with extra care; the Method page shows the back-test.

contest.choosing_rule: Rules whose P10-P90 ranges caught the actual total in 75% to 85% of back-test cases are eligible. Among them the lowest median absolute error is the best; the simplest eligible rule within 5% of that error wins. If no rule is eligible, the rule whose coverage is closest to 80% wins. This rule was fixed in assumptions/backtest.yaml before any score was computed.

rules.name: average of the six rules
rules.describe: simple average of last_5_mean, last_3_mean, median_5, damped_trend, shrink_to_group, top_down_share

bias_correction.rule: Keep the P50 pool-ratio correction only if, out of time, its median absolute error is lower than the uncorrected projection's and its P10-P90 coverage is inside 75%-85%; otherwise drop it. Fixed in assumptions/backtest.yaml (bias_correction) before any score was computed.
bias_correction.reason: the correction did not lower the out-of-time error

variants.definition: all years: every county-year in the Building Permits Survey files, including figures the Census Bureau imputed for offices that did not report; observed only: county-years with any imputed figure removed from both the history a rule reads and the target years it is scored on

statewide.definition: the same rules applied to the state's yearly totals (counties that did not report a year left out of that year); one case per origin; each case's P10-P90 range from the other origins' ratios

origins.note: The 21 rolling origins overlap: each shares up to 4 of its 5 target years with the next. They hold about 5 non-overlapping 5-year periods, so case counts overstate the independent evidence; read coverage and error as resting on about 5 periods, not 21.

stress.sentence: If the next five years look like the 10 past boom periods (origins 1999, 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019), the baseline's likely range is 4,706 units to 15,169 units (middle 10,090 units).

findings: 7 rules were back-tested on the same 473 county cases. The three-year mean won: it was typically 66% off, its ranges caught the real total in 60% of cases, and it ran 6% low on average. No rule's coverage was inside the band, so the closest to 80% won.
The five-year mean was typically 67% off and ran 4% low.

Out of time (each origin corrected only with errors known by then; 315 cases), the winner's own projection was typically 64% off. Correcting it by size class gave 90% with ranges that caught 62%; by place type, 104% and 57%. The engine uses size-class pools: place-type pools did not lower the out-of-time error.
Ranges built from past errors caught the real total less often when tested on later years than when tested on other counties: a new housing cycle moves every county at once.

The winner was chosen on the whole back-test (every origin at once), so the choice itself is in-sample; its ranges and the corrections are scored only with errors from earlier origins. Size classes are worked out at each origin from the years up to it; place types are today's county grouping (current data) applied to every origin.

In 'Rural, growing, more homes in low-income tax-credit tracts' counties the five-year mean ran 37% high and the three-year mean runs 1% low; its ranges caught 10 of 15 cases. Few cases: read this as a few places, not a pattern.
In 'Rural, slow-growth, lower-cost' counties the five-year mean ran 43% high and the three-year mean runs 23% high; its ranges caught 58 of 115 cases.

In counties with a higher share of Qualified Census Tracts the five-year mean ran 33% high and the three-year mean runs 9% high; its ranges caught 30 of 45 cases. Few cases: read this as a few places, not a pattern.

disclosures.selection_measured: Measured by a pre-registered nested test that re-chooses the rule at each start year from matured cases only, with permit-only place types: assumptions/calibration/nested_selection.yaml (visionhousing validate-nested-selection; docs/modules/validation_nested_selection.md).

cards.study: State confidence check (current range method, held out of time)
cards.method: The state's own state-total error record blended toward Pennsylvania's, only widened, scored with one fixed rule for every state (not each state's shipped rule).
cards.target: Five-year total of units authorized by building permits in the state (national BPS county panel)

release.data: U.S. Census Bureau, Building Permits Survey, county annual files, 1990-2025

origin_set.note: Consecutive start years share all but one of their five target years; see scores.non_overlapping for start years five years apart.

disclosures.selection_full_record: The projection rule each study scores (and the baseline's bias-correction and widening settings) was chosen on the full record, which includes the evaluation years of every fold, so the counts are somewhat favourable. Not rebuilt now.
disclosures.present_day_place_types: Not used by this card's ranges (the scored rule needs no place types).
disclosures.selection_measured: Measured by a pre-registered nested test that re-chooses the rule at each start year from matured cases only, with permit-only place types: assumptions/calibration/nested_selection.yaml (visionhousing validate-nested-selection; docs/modules/validation_nested_selection.md).
